content.text: Time III: Introduction to Generalist Time Markers and Time

Time in Okinawan is the exact same as Japanese. Traditionally, Okinawan never cared about precise times, so there was no clock system. There was a slightly more precise system but not as precise as now back then as well, but that is a thing for the advanced course. Therefore, if you have been taking a Japanese course or have already learned some Japanese, you should know that it is 〜時〜分。

Additionally when you say "At [time/date/year]" you add に like Japanese. Many people make the mistake of using んかい here, but that is incorrect, and it would've costed a few points off the しまくとぅば９級 exam back when it existed. That is not good for you.
e.g., 三月（さんぐゎち）に = At March etc.
